status: REGISTERED 2026-11-18 before any recorded run; after tests/check_seed_select.cu (6,000 cases; two mutants rejected), tests/check_range_prune.py on cuda_range_prune_ts, a full-collection VERIFY=1 check of 10 queries at range sizes 256 and 1024, and smoke test dev-ts-01 (DEV=1, no fixtures or correctness, 1 process, 1 warm-up + 1 round) passed every stage. No latency from this experiment was read before registration
recording: self-contained runtime gate (code/gate.py, a copy of experiments/2026-11-18-range-pruning/code/gate.py (amendments 1 and 3)) and self-recorded manifests; not recorded by the team runtime
question: Does a faster seed selection (fewer radix passes, warp-aggregated histograms, block scans, coalesced tiled placement) make the term-major pruned scorer faster, with the same seeds, schedule and answers?
hypothesis: The full-collection profile (run 20261118-cuda5-profile-01) measured select_seeds at 21.9 / 48.3 us per query (range size 1024 / 256) in one thread block, stalled on barriers (thread 0 walks 256 bins in each of four passes) and on uncoalesced loads (contiguous per-thread chunks in the placement pass). The new kernel needs two 12-bit histogram passes for typical queries and one coalesced placement pass, so prunets should be faster than prunetb at both sizes, more so at 256
contract: GSP-CAP32-U32GUARDED-NUMERIC-TIES-v1; uint8 impacts, prepared integer query weights, uint32 accumulation under the conservative-bound guard, reported as uint64; ties by original numeric passage ID; all passages eligible
exactness: select_seeds selects the same set, the min(S, ranges) largest bounds with ties to the lower range index: its radix digits start at the bit length of the query's conservative bound sum(weight) * 255 * multiplicity, which no range bound exceeds (every bound is a sum of weight * block max * multiplicity over a subset of the query's terms, block max <= 255). Bounds, theta, the scored set and the answers are therefore identical to cuda_range_prune_tb. Seeds are placed in range order instead of atomic order; the merge is order-independent

inputs.rule: checked by whole-file SHA-256 before any scoring
inputs.provenance: W512 and W256 built on cuda5 from the pinned GSP by range_bitpack_tool (`build GSP OUT SIZE positions`, uniform ranges), compiled from src/range_bitpack_tool.cpp and src/range_bitpack.h as last changed in 223cf4b; the same binary regenerated the pinned W1024 index with an equal hash

fixed.host: cuda5 (RTX 4070, UUID GPU-ab7b89ba-5664-fd05-e352-a4bc034e5ff7; host thread on CPU 0, local allocation)

implementations.v2: src/cuda_range_v2.cu unchanged (variant 5): one block per range, exhaustive
implementations.prunetb: src/cuda_range_prune_tb.cu unchanged: the scorer measured in term-major bounds run 20261118-cuda5-tb-01 (the project's pruned scorer by that run's decision rule)
implementations.prunets: src/cuda_range_prune_ts.cu: cuda_range_prune_tb.cu with step 2 (select_seeds) replaced: 12-bit radix digits from the per-query bound bit length (host-computed, passed as a kernel argument), warp-aggregated shared-memory histogram atomics (__match_any_sync), digit found by a block scan, seeds placed by a block scan over coalesced 4096-bound tiles with early exit; one block of 1024 threads as before. Everything else identical, plus an RBP_NO_MAIN guard for the unit test
implementations.prior_binaries: cuda_range_v2, cuda_range_prune_tb and range_bitpack_tool are the binaries of run 20261118-cuda5-tb-01, copied after checking their hashes against its record and that their sources are unchanged; their fixtures are that run's (not repeated); correctness is repeated here

timing_boundary: Per query, host wall clock from building the query argument from its parsed (term, weight) pairs to the ordered top-k (original IDs and scores) in host memory, including every kernel launch, synchronisation and the result transfer (query_wall_ms, unchanged from v2). The pruned scorer's schedule statistics are copied after the boundary. Index loading, block maxima, tie ranks, the gate, output writes and checks are outside it

timing.order: every configuration once per pass, three passes with rotation offsets 0, ceil(n/3), ceil(2n/3)
timing.before_each_process: timing processes only: wait (30 s polls, bounded by the deadline) until no foreign GPU process is active, 7000 MiB of device memory are free and other users' CPU use is at most CPU_LIMIT cores
timing.sampling: every 0.5 s during each process: nvidia-smi compute processes on the GPU and machine CPU time from /proc minus the scorer and the sampler; sampler on CPU 15
timing.eligibility: a timing process is ineligible if a foreign GPU process was active (per-process SM or memory utilisation above 0, or listed but not reported) in its released phase, its own was not sampled, or other users' CPU use averaged more than CPU_LIMIT cores; a non-zero exit while another GPU process was sampled is a contended failure (ineligible); any other failure stops the run
timing.replacement: ineligible processes are kept under raw/ineligible/ and replaced without a count limit; the run stops at a 12-hour deadline and can be resumed from the same commit
timing.cpu_limit_rationale: Every configuration is a GPU scorer with one host thread on CPU 0 (sampler on CPU 15, 14 other cores). The earlier GPU experiments (range batching, full-collection baselines) had no CPU rule. The CPU-baseline experiment's 1.0 core was first adopted here, but in dry-run dev-prune-01 another user's single-threaded job kept other CPU use at 1.1-2.7 cores for over 15 minutes with no GPU process, which would stall or fail the run without bearing on GPU timing. 4.0 cores is a quarter of the machine. It was set before registration and before any latency from this experiment was read; other users' CPU use is recorded for every process. The GPU rule (no other GPU process sampled) is unchanged
timing.rules_source: the range-pruning experiment's rules with its amendments 1-3 in force from the start

correctness_gate: From the timed source and binaries on the timed host: tests/check_seed_select.cu (select_seeds against a host sort on 6,000 adversarial cases) and tests/check_range_prune.py for cuda_range_prune_ts (answers and the independent schedule model); two deliberate gate rejections; every configuration once against the CPU reference, with VERIFY=1 (host recomputation of every answer and of the whole schedule) for the two prunets configurations; every timing process's answers against the CPU reference; per-query schedules of prunetb and prunets identical (analysis). Any mismatch stops the run

analysis.primary: prunetb-w<size>-s64 / prunets-w<size>-s64 for size 1024 and 256: geometric mean over (process, query) pairs; above 1 means the fast seed selection is faster
analysis.secondary: v2-w1024 / prunets-w<size>-s64 (overall speedup over the exact range scorer); replication of the term-major bounds secondary contrasts v2-w1024 / prunetb-w<size>-s64
analysis.descriptive: median, mean, p95, p99 of the query-process medians; scored range fraction and postings per query of each pruned configuration (deterministic; checked identical across rounds, processes, and between prunetb and prunets)
analysis.interval: crossed process/query bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 20261118, percentile 2.5/97.5; conditional on this session and the calibration queries

decision_rule: prunets replaces prunetb as the project's pruned scorer if a primary interval lies wholly above 1 (identical seeds, schedule and answers, so no other trade-off); otherwise prunetb is kept and the result reported as negative
limits: one host, one GPU (RTX 4070), k=10, batch 1
